```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern unit-of-work
 * @options dc40e1d26184fc82
 */

/**
 * The Order collection: its minimum record, its name, and a typed accessor.
 *
 * The machinery lives in `unit-of-work-core` and is shared with every other
 * entity. Adding a second entity means a second file like this one, not a
 * second copy of that.
 */

import type {
  CollectionSpec,
  NewRecord,
  Tracked,
  UnitOfWork,
} from "../lib/core.js";

/**
 * What `Order` must have for this module to track it.
 *
 * Your own `Order` satisfies this by having an `id` and a `version`, so nothing
 * here needs to know the rest of its fields. That is deliberate: a generated
 * file that declared your domain type would have to be edited every time the
 * domain changed, and regenerating it would then overwrite the edit.
 *
 * The key is a plain `string`. `branded-type` is how it stops being
 * interchangeable with every other entity's key, and the change is confined to
 * this file.
 */
export interface OrderRecord {
  readonly id: string;
  /**
   * Assigned on insert and incremented on every update by the unit of work,
   * never by you.
   */
  readonly version: number;
}

/**
 * Where Order records live.
 *
 * Exported so that a datastore adapter can be told which collections exist
 * without importing every entity's accessor.
 */
export const ORDERS_COLLECTION = "orders";

/**
 * Tracking orders in one unit of work.
 *
 * Generic in your own `Order`, so every method is typed in terms of your type
 * rather than the minimum this file declares.
 */
export interface OrderTracking<T extends OrderRecord> {
  /**
   * The record under this key, or `undefined` if there is none.
   */
  load(id: T["id"]): Promise<Tracked<T, "id"> | undefined>;
  /**
   * The record under this key, or an error naming what was missing.
   */
  require(id: T["id"]): Promise<Tracked<T, "id">>;
  /**
   * Track a new record, to be inserted at commit.
   */
  add(record: NewRecord<T, "id">): Tracked<T, "id">;
}

/**
 * What the machinery needs to know about orders, at your own record type.
 *
 * A function rather than a constant because it is specific to the `T` you use
 * it at, and a constant would have to be declared at one of them. `orders`
 * calls it, and so does anything that has to name this collection to something
 * entity-independent — an in-memory store's fixtures, for one.
 */
export function orderCollectionSpec<T extends OrderRecord>(): CollectionSpec<
  T,
  "id"
> {
  return { collection: ORDERS_COLLECTION, keyField: "id" };
}

/**
 * Track orders in `uow`.
 *
 * Pass your domain type: `orders<Order>(uow)`.
 */
export function orders<T extends OrderRecord>(
  uow: UnitOfWork,
): OrderTracking<T> {
  const spec = orderCollectionSpec<T>();

  return {
    load: (id) => uow.load<T, "id">(spec, id),
    require: (id) => uow.require<T, "id">(spec, id),
    add: (record) => uow.add<T, "id">(spec, record),
  };
}
```
